title: So I heard dynamic weather systems are all the hype right now
author: Oli4K
selftext:
It started with a single cloud, which grew into a somewhat more complete cloud cover generator, but after reading into [how clouds actually work](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/an-introduction-to-clouds/4ACE9495269508EE27AC407F98CEFDAF) I decided the clouds in my radio control soaring sim needed a home that would feel natural to them.   
  
For the sake of time the sky in this video are severely sped up. The quick changes in cloud cover are a result of changing the settings. Cloud variables (most but not all are exposed in the debug UI) are stored in configuration that's tweaked for each location. Shadows are generated in a reasonably cheap way but have difficulty keeping up when time advance is more than 1x. I have had a few optimisation steps to make transition between the LOD cloud transitions stable, added caching and making sure the render pipeline was efficient. I let the more expensive models handle that work.

Next step is adding dynamic weather drivers, which is being built at the moment. That will be optional and follows 'forecasts' that remain flyable, as it would be pointless to have bad weather in a flight sim. The system supports cumulus clouds now, driven by humidity, temperature and dew temperature, and shaped by wind which is a separate system. Terrain also influences clouds so they can't pass through, although the level in the video is flat so there it is not an issue.  
  
Other cloud types can be added later. As can higher quality settings with more detail. Dynamic weather transitions are built and ready for testing. All in all the project is getting more complex, but it remains quite flexible and extensible. Although keeping it that way may come with new challenges.

It's probably nowhere near what GTA6 can do, but for less than $20 in credits and about a few days of work I'm quite pleased with it so far.
